Command: Bring an ascending and descending offering according to means
Summary: The command: Bring an ascending and descending offering according to means (Leviticus 5:7). The offering slid with the sinner's means: lamb or goat, two birds, or fine flour for the very poor, so no one was shut out from atonement.
Commandment: Bring an ascending and descending offering according to means, as prescribed in Leviticus 5:7.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: The offering slid with the sinner's means: lamb or goat, two birds, or fine flour for the very poor, so no one was shut out from atonement — a ceremonial law of the open door. Its goal was to make atonement reachable at every level of wealth. The evil was exclusion by poverty, the poor sinner left without a sacrifice he could afford. It restrained that by the sliding scale: the offering descended to meet the giver, and no one was priced out of forgiveness.
